questions.prompt: Case study, Northwind Assist. Which three telemetry elements are most important for the required end-to-end audit trail? Choose three.
options: Per-service request and error totals aggregated by hour without a shared operation identifier
Retrieved document and chunk identifiers retained as source-provenance metadata
The final answer, total duration, and token count without retrieval, tool, or approval events
Approval request, reviewer decision, and resulting action events retained in the same trace
Correlated trace spans for model, retrieval, and tool operations under one operation identifier
answer: Correlated trace spans for model, retrieval, and tool operations under one operation identifier
Retrieved document and chunk identifiers retained as source-provenance metadata
Approval request, reviewer decision, and resulting action events retained in the same trace
questions.explain: A useful agent audit connects the model, retrieval, and tool spans, preserves evidence provenance, and records human approvals. A final answer alone cannot explain how the action occurred.
questions.teach: An end-to-end audit trail lets you reconstruct a conversation after the fact. It needs connected traces across the model, retrieval and tool steps, identifiers for the evidence that was retrieved, and records of approval requests and decisions. Totals and final answers on their own cannot show how an action came about.
hints: The requirement lists what must be traceable: retrievals, model responses, tool arguments, tool results, approvals and correlation identifiers. Read the options against that list.
Aggregates by hour, or only the final answer with duration and token count, lose the individual steps that an auditor wants to follow.
The three right telemetry elements are linked: a connected record of the operations, the identity of the evidence used, and the human decisions along the way.
questions.deep: Use one operation or conversation ID across the app, Foundry and Search so Application Insights can join them. Keep sensitive text out of spans where identifiers are enough. Microsoft Learn: Foundry agent tracing, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/observability/how-to/trace-agent-setup

questions.prompt: Case study, Northwind Assist. Northwind separates deployment automation from the running support application. The application only invokes the support agent and reads the approved policy index. Which production assignment best satisfies least privilege?
options: Give the application Foundry User at the resource scope and Search Service Contributor on the search service
Give the application Cognitive Services Contributor and Search Service Contributor at the resource-group scope
Give the application Foundry Agent Consumer at the agent scope and Search Index Data Reader on the policy index or search service
Give the application Reader on the Foundry project and Search Index Data Contributor on the policy index
answer: Give the application Foundry Agent Consumer at the agent scope and Search Index Data Reader on the policy index or search service
questions.explain: A runtime identity needs only agent endpoint interaction and index query permissions. Foundry Agent Consumer plus Search Index Data Reader provides those data-plane capabilities at narrow scopes.
questions.teach: Least privilege means granting only the permissions a workload needs, at the smallest scope that works. A runtime application that only talks to an agent and queries an index needs an interaction role for the agent and a read role for the index, not roles for building agents or managing services.
hints: Write down what the running application does: it invokes one agent, and it reads documents from one index. Nothing in that list builds, deploys or administers anything.
Roles that let a principal create or manage resources, or that apply at resource-group scope, give far more than the list needs. A read-only management role does not allow calling the agent.
Pick the pair of assignments that matches exactly those two actions, scoped as narrowly as each service allows.
questions.deep: Keep deployment automation on a different identity from the runtime app, as the case does, so a compromise of the app cannot change resources. Search distinguishes data-plane roles for reading and writing index content from service-management roles. Microsoft Learn: Role-based access control for Microsoft Foundry, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry

questions.case:
Alpine Media Library. Multimodal content discovery and compliance.

OVERVIEW
Alpine Ski House owns a rapidly growing media library used by product, accessibility, legal, and localization teams. The library contains approved product photography, draft artwork, marketing videos, audio narration, and PDF storyboards from internal and external contributors.
Editors currently search separate file shares by filename and often cannot locate an asset when they remember only its subject or campaign. Alpine wants one search experience that supports exact identifiers, natural-language discovery, and evidence-grounded answers about visual content.
A new assistant will generate accessible descriptions, answer questions about visible evidence, and extract a consistent campaign record from every supported media type. Human editors remain responsible for approving generated descriptions and any edited asset before publication.

DATA

questions.prompt: Case study, Alpine Media Library. What should Alpine configure to reuse one extraction definition that processes PDFs and returns campaign fields plus a Markdown representation?

questions.prompt: Case study, Alpine Media Library. Which three query capabilities should be combined to meet Alpine's search requirements? Choose three.
options: Faceted navigation over product and campaign fields without semantic or vector retrieval
Full-text keyword search to preserve exact product names, codes, and phrases
Semantic reranking applied to the merged keyword and vector result set
Vector search over campaign content to retrieve conceptually similar material
A scoring profile that boosts recently modified documents after a keyword-only query
answer: Full-text keyword search to preserve exact product names, codes, and phrases
Vector search over campaign content to retrieve conceptually similar material
Semantic reranking applied to the merged keyword and vector result set
questions.explain: Keyword search preserves exact product-code matches, vector search adds conceptual similarity, and semantic ranking reranks text-rich results from the hybrid result set.
questions.teach: Azure AI Search can combine query styles. questions.deep: Keep the product-code field out of analyzers that tokenise or stem it, so exact matching survives. Semantic ranking works best on text-rich fields and reranks only the top results. questions.prompt: Case study, Alpine Media Library. Which architecture best meets Alpine's security requirement?
options: Use public endpoints restricted by service firewalls and authenticate each workload with managed identity
Private endpoints, disabled public network access where supported, private DNS, and managed-identity RBAC
Use VNet integration for the application subnet while leaving each AI service on its public endpoint
Use private endpoints and private DNS but authenticate every workload with one centrally rotated service key

questions.prompt: Case study, Alpine Media Library. Alpine receives visually varied campaign PDFs and images. It needs one reusable definition with natural-language field descriptions, Markdown content, and source-grounded values without first labeling examples. Which starting point is most appropriate?
options: An Azure AI Search indexer using only the OCR and Split skills
A Document Intelligence custom neural model trained from labeled campaign examples
A custom Content Understanding analyzer with a field schema and detailed output
A Document Intelligence prebuilt layout model followed by application-written field rules
answer: A custom Content Understanding analyzer with a field schema and detailed output
questions.explain: Content Understanding is the best fit for varied multimodal inputs and fields described in natural language. Detailed output preserves the evidence needed for review.
questions.teach: Choose between Document Intelligence and Content Understanding by the inputs and the setup you can afford. Choose the starting point whose configuration is a field schema with natural-language descriptions plus detailed output, since that combination covers reuse, Markdown, grounding and the lack of labelled examples.
questions.deep: Start with a small schema and a handful of representative files, and check confidence and grounding before scaling. questions.case:
Fabrikam Claims Hub. Multimodal insurance-claim intake and review.

OVERVIEW
Fabrikam Insurance receives automobile claims through brokers, mobile applications, email, and call centers. A single claim can include standardized claim forms, repair estimates, photographs, police reports, medical notes, and recorded conversations.
Adjusters currently copy information between systems and manually compare documents for conflicting dates, amounts, and policy identifiers. Fabrikam wants a claims assistant that assembles an evidence package, highlights discrepancies, and recommends the next review step without making a payment decision.
The planned solution uses a Microsoft Foundry project, Azure AI Search, Azure Content Understanding, Document Intelligence, Azure Speech, and an internal claims API. The rollout begins with automobile claims and may later include property claims with substantially different document layouts.

DATA
The primary claim form has a stable layout and an existing Document Intelligence prebuilt or custom model can extract its standard fields efficiently. Other submissions, including medical narratives and broker correspondence, are highly variable and can require inferred fields described in natural language.
Repair estimates contain tables, line items, signatures, selection marks, handwritten additions, and policy identifiers. Scans vary in quality. Reviewers need both structured fields and layout-aware text so they can confirm how an extracted value relates to its surrounding document content.
Claim photographs can contain license plates, damage indicators, shop labels, and untrusted text. The solution must associate visual findings with the source image and must not obey instructions embedded in photographed signs, notes, or uploaded screenshots.
Recorded calls arrive in Azure Blob Storage overnight. Some files exceed the duration suitable for a real-time request. Reviewers require timestamps, speaker labels, transcription status, and links from extracted evidence back to the supporting page, image, or media segment.

REQUIREMENTS
The extraction output must conform to a stable JSON schema and include confidence or grounding information plus source locations. Fields include claimant identity, incident date, policy number, estimated loss, currency, repair lines, injuries, and a collection of detected inconsistencies.
Fabrikam should use the document-processing tool that best matches each workload. Standardized forms favor supported prebuilt or trained Document Intelligence models, while varied unstructured or multimodal evidence should use Content Understanding analyzers and their schema-based outputs.
Low-confidence fields, missing required evidence, and conflicts between documents must route the claim to a human reviewer. The assistant can explain the conflict and draft a recommendation, but it cannot silently choose one source as authoritative when policy requires review.
Payments above EUR 20,000 require explicit adjuster approval before the payment tool is called. Every payment request includes a claim identifier and idempotency key. Retrying after a network timeout must return the original result or safely resume instead of issuing a duplicate payment.
Historical calls must be transcribed asynchronously in bulk. Claim photos must be screened for unsafe content and indirect prompt injection. All indexed evidence must retain the tenant, claim, document, page, and media-segment identifiers required for filtering and citation.

SECURITY
All services use private endpoints where supported, and public access is disabled for production resources. Production applications use managed identities and narrowly scoped data-plane roles; API keys are not stored in application settings.
Claims are partitioned by business unit and jurisdiction. Search queries must apply the authorization filter before vector scoring so that evidence from another tenant or jurisdiction cannot enter the candidate set.
Every extraction request, retrieval, model response, tool argument, payment result, confidence-based routing decision, and human approval is retained for audit with a shared correlation identifier. Sensitive document contents must not be written to diagnostic logs unnecessarily. The release gate uses a labeled evaluation set containing clean forms, noisy scans, unusual narratives, contradictory evidence, and long recordings. Fabrikam measures field accuracy, confidence calibration, citation correctness, tenant isolation, transcription completion, and duplicate-payment prevention. A new analyzer or model version cannot advance when it improves average extraction but materially worsens a protected claim category or removes reviewer-verifiable grounding.
questions.prompt: Case study, Fabrikam Claims Hub. Which three controls should Fabrikam implement to meet its production security and audit requirements? Choose three.
options: Store the claims API key in a centrally managed project connection that is available to every claims agent
Assign the application's managed identity Contributor on each production resource group to simplify access
Correlate retrieval, generation, tool, and approval events in trace records
Use managed identities with minimum required data-plane roles
Use private endpoints and private DNS for supported service connections
answer: Use managed identities with minimum required data-plane roles
Use private endpoints and private DNS for supported service connections
Correlate retrieval, generation, tool, and approval events in trace records
questions.explain: Managed identities with minimum data-plane roles remove stored credentials, private endpoints with private DNS keep traffic on private paths, and correlated traces of retrieval, generation, tool and approval events provide the audit trail. A shared key connection and Contributor on resource groups both violate least privilege.
questions.teach: A production security and audit design rests on three ideas. Identities replace stored secrets: managed identities with narrowly scoped data-plane roles. Network paths are private: private endpoints with private DNS, and public access disabled. Activity is traceable: events from retrieval, generation, tools and approvals are linked by a shared identifier.
hints: The case asks for production security and audit. Group the options by which requirement they serve: how the app authenticates, how traffic reaches the services, and how actions are recorded.

A key stored in a shared connection that every agent can use is a stored secret with wide reach, and a broad Contributor role on resource groups is far more than the app needs. Both go against the case's security section.
The three controls to choose map onto the three groups: an identity design, a network design and a logging design.
questions.deep: The case also says sensitive document contents should not be written to diagnostic logs unnecessarily, so log identifiers and hashes rather than raw text. A correlation ID that appears in every service's logs is what makes the audit trail joinable. Microsoft Learn: Authentication and authorization in Microsoft Foundry, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/authentication-authorization-foundry

questions.prompt: Case study, Fabrikam Claims Hub. How should Fabrikam implement a payment recommendation that might be retried after a transient failure?
options: Treat an approved model confidence threshold as payment authorization and query the backend after execution
Pause for adjuster approval, then call the payment service without an idempotency key and disable automatic retries
Call the payment service after approval but generate a new request identifier whenever a timed-out call is retried
Pause for adjuster approval when required, then call a validated payment service with an idempotency key
answer: Pause for adjuster approval when required, then call a validated payment service with an idempotency key

questions.deep: The key should be generated once per intended payment and stored with the request before the first attempt, so a restart reuses it. The service stores the outcome against the key and returns it on repeats. Workflows that pause for approval are a preview capability. questions.prompt: Case study, Fabrikam Claims Hub. Which Speech capability should Fabrikam use for the overnight archive of call recordings?
options: Batch transcription submitted from Blob Storage with diarization and timestamp options
Run continuous real-time recognition workers for every stored recording until the entire archive completes
Use conversation transcription sessions for the stored files and keep every session open until processing finishes

questions.prompt: Case study, Fabrikam Claims Hub. Which three analyzer settings or outputs directly support Fabrikam's extraction requirements? Choose three.

Per-field confidence values and source-location details
Use a layout analyzer without a business-field schema and infer all claim values later from plain text
Declare the required field schema but disable detailed output so confidence and source locations are omitted
Document content and layout output suitable for grounding and reviewer display

questions.prompt: Case study, Fabrikam Claims Hub. Fabrikam can identify a subset of uploads as standard vendor invoices before analysis. For that subset it needs invoice totals, dates, vendors, and line items with the least custom configuration. What should the routing workflow invoke first?

The Document Intelligence prebuilt invoice model
The Document Intelligence prebuilt layout model plus handwritten parsing rules
A custom Content Understanding analyzer for every standard invoice

Pick the tool that is specifically built for this document type and works out of the box, since the routing step has already decided that these uploads are standard invoices.

questions.case:
Contoso Field Service. A multilingual agent for industrial technicians.

OVERVIEW
Contoso technicians service industrial pumps, compressors, and control systems across Europe. They often work in noisy locations with limited access to a laptop and need a voice-enabled assistant that can retrieve manuals, interpret equipment photographs, and prepare work orders.
The assistant is hosted in Microsoft Foundry and is accessed from a mobile application. It retrieves approved manuals from Azure AI Search and uses an internal REST API to create or update work orders after the technician confirms the proposed action.
The initial release covers four equipment families and four spoken languages. Contoso expects the knowledge base and model deployments to be reused by additional regional projects, while project data and technician conversations remain isolated.

SEARCH AND TOOLS
Manuals contain exact error codes, diagrams, part identifiers, revision dates, and equipment-family metadata. Some codes contain punctuation that must remain intact for exact lookup, while conceptual questions require lexical and vector retrieval over explanatory text.
The search index stores human-readable chunks and corresponding vectors. Equipment family, revision status, language, and effective date are filterable. Search results must exclude obsolete manuals and favor the latest approved revision for the technician's selected equipment.
The work-order API publishes an OpenAPI 3.1 document. Each operation has a unique operationId, a bounded JSON schema, and Microsoft Entra authentication. Create and reschedule operations can change production systems and therefore require confirmation.
The Foundry project uses connections for Search and the work-order API. Connections should be centrally manageable where reuse is required, but developers should receive access only to the project and resources needed for their regional workload.

INTERACTION
Technicians speak English, French, German, and Italian. They need interim transcripts during live conversations and translated text when a manual is available only in another supported language. The application must preserve technical codes without translating them.
The mobile client sends audio continuously and displays partial recognition results before the final utterance. Historical recordings are not part of the interactive path and can use a separate asynchronous transcription workflow when required.
When a technician uploads a control-panel photograph, the answer must be based only on visible indicators, labels, and grounded manual evidence. If the image is blurred or omits a required component, the assistant must ask for another photograph instead of guessing.
The agent keeps conversation state for the active maintenance session. Tool outputs and retrieved evidence are associated with that session, and a new technician or work order must not inherit the previous session's private context.
Before a state-changing tool call, the application presents the equipment identifier, proposed operation, and arguments for confirmation. Read-only diagnostic lookups do not require the same approval step but still appear in the trace.

OPERATIONS
Inference must remain in the EU data zone. Workload volume is steady during weekday shifts, and interactive latency must be predictable. Contoso is willing to reserve capacity if that is more appropriate than relying on variable shared throughput.
The operations team needs traces that separate speech recognition, retrieval, generation, and work-order tool latency. It also monitors token usage, failed tool calls, throttling, retrieval relevance, and the proportion of sessions escalated for insufficient evidence.
The production application uses managed identity and keyless credentials. A valid token with insufficient scope should be diagnosed as an authorization problem, while throttling should use bounded retries with exponential backoff rather than immediate repeated requests. Support runbooks distinguish malformed endpoints, unknown deployment names, expired or wrongly scoped tokens, network name-resolution failures, invalid tool payloads, and service throttling. Every retry preserves the correlation and idempotency identifiers. A canary evaluation set covers noisy speech, punctuation-heavy error codes, blurred photographs, obsolete manuals, and rejected work-order confirmations before a regional project receives a new workflow version.
questions.prompt: Case study, Contoso Field Service. Which deployment option best meets Contoso's EU processing and predictable-latency requirements for a steady workload?
options: Regional Provisioned in one EU region without the required EU data-zone deployment scope
Global Provisioned with reserved capacity that can process requests outside the EU data zone
Data Zone Provisioned with capacity sized for the workload
Data Zone Standard with pay-per-token capacity and dynamic quota enabled
answer: Data Zone Provisioned with capacity sized for the workload
questions.explain: Data Zone Provisioned keeps inference within the selected US or EU data zone and supplies dedicated provisioned capacity for predictable throughput and latency. The other choices do not satisfy both requirements.
questions.teach: A deployment type combines a scope and a capacity model. Scope says where processing may happen: globally, inside a data zone such as the EU, or inside one region. Capacity model says whether you pay per token or reserve throughput, which provides predictable latency for steady workloads. Both requirements have to be satisfied together.
hints: The case gives two requirements: inference stays in the EU data zone, and latency must be predictable for steady weekday traffic where reserving capacity is acceptable. Treat them as two separate filters.

Apply the location filter first. Anything that may process requests outside the EU zone is out, however good its capacity model is. A single region is stricter than the requirement and not the same as the EU zone.
Apply the capacity filter to what remains. Pay-per-token capacity shares throughput, while reserved capacity gives the predictability the case wants.
questions.deep: Provisioned throughput is purchased in provisioned throughput units, and its cost is fixed whether or not you use it. That is why the case's steady weekday load, rather than bursty traffic, is the clue that reserving is sensible. Microsoft Learn: Provisioned throughput for Foundry Models, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/provisioned-throughput

questions.prompt: Case study, Contoso Field Service. Which three actions should Contoso take when connecting the work-order API as an agent tool? Choose three.
options: Store a permanent function key in the project connection and restrict the tool through its OpenAPI description
Register the OpenAPI specification with a unique operationId for each callable operation
Validate arguments and require confirmation before schedule-changing operations
Use a project connection and managed identity where supported
Describe argument limits in the agent instructions and let the model bypass backend validation after confirmation
answer: Register the OpenAPI specification with a unique operationId for each callable operation
Use a project connection and managed identity where supported
Validate arguments and require confirmation before schedule-changing operations
questions.explain: Foundry OpenAPI tools require usable operation identifiers. A managed-identity project connection avoids embedded secrets, and deterministic argument validation plus confirmation constrains high-impact calls.
questions.teach: When an agent calls an API through an OpenAPI tool, three things matter. Each callable operation needs a unique operationId so the tool can name it. Authentication should come from a managed project connection and identity instead of secrets in the description. For operations that change production systems, arguments are validated by your code and a person confirms the action.
hints: The case describes the work-order API: each operation has an identifier, uses Microsoft Entra authentication, and some operations change production systems. Turn those facts into the three actions asked for.

A permanent key stored for the tool, or relying on the model to respect limits written in its instructions, replaces real controls with trust. Letting the model skip validation after confirmation also removes a safeguard.
The right actions cover how the tool is described, how it authenticates, and how risky calls are checked and confirmed.
questions.deep: Keep read-only lookups free of approval but still traced, as the case says, so confirmation requests stay rare and meaningful. Validate against the same schema the specification declares, on the server that executes the call. Microsoft Learn: OpenAPI tools for Foundry agents, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/openapi

questions.prompt: Case study, Contoso Field Service. How should the agent answer a technician who asks whether a warning light is active in an uploaded control-panel photo?
options: Use OCR on panel labels, retrieve the matching manual page, and infer the light state without visual reasoning

Train an object detector for warning lights and always return the detected class without an uncertainty path

answer: Use a multimodal model with the photo and question, require evidence-based output, and request a clearer image when uncertain
questions.explain: A multimodal model can reason over the supplied image. Instructions should constrain the response to visible evidence and define an uncertainty path so the agent asks for better evidence rather than fabricating a state.
questions.teach: Answering questions about a technician's photo is a job for a multimodal model that sees the image. questions.deep: Put the uncertainty behaviour into both the prompt and the evaluation set, including deliberately blurred photos. questions.prompt: Case study, Contoso Field Service. Arrange the live multilingual interaction stages in the correct order.
tray: Capture the live audio stream
Translate recognized text into the technician's target language
Produce interim and final speech-recognition results
Optionally synthesize the translated response with the selected voice
answer: Capture the live audio stream
Produce interim and final speech-recognition results
Translate recognized text into the technician's target language
Optionally synthesize the translated response with the selected voice
questions.explain: The application first captures and recognizes speech, then translates recognized text, and can finally synthesize translated output. Streaming recognition provides the interim results required during the conversation.
questions.teach: A live multilingual interaction runs as a stream. Audio is captured, recognized with interim results that update as the person speaks, and the recognized text is translated. hints: Follow the data from the technician's mouth to the screen or speaker. Audio comes first, text comes next, then a different language, and finally optionally sound again.
Translation works on recognized text, so it cannot precede recognition. Synthesis is described as optional and works on translated text, so it cannot precede translation.
Start with whatever supplies the raw input, since nothing else can happen until it exists, and finish with the step that the scenario itself describes as optional.
questions.deep: The Speech SDK's translation recognizer performs recognition and translation together and can return synthesized audio, but the logical order stays the same. Technical codes should be protected from translation, as the case requires. questions.prompt: Case study, Contoso Field Service. Which four search capabilities should Contoso combine for manual retrieval? Choose four.
options: Use hybrid retrieval but apply the equipment and revision authorization filters only after vector scoring
Vector search that retrieves instructions with conceptually similar technical meaning
Semantic reranking applied after reciprocal-rank fusion of keyword and vector results
Full-text search that preserves exact matches for error codes and part identifiers
A pre-scoring filter for equipment family, approval state, and effective revision
Use semantic keyword search without vectors and boost every document from the selected equipment family
answer: Full-text search that preserves exact matches for error codes and part identifiers
Vector search that retrieves instructions with conceptually similar technical meaning
A pre-scoring filter for equipment family, approval state, and effective revision
Semantic reranking applied after reciprocal-rank fusion of keyword and vector results
questions.explain: Hybrid retrieval combines full-text and vector results, a pre-scoring filter restricts results to the right equipment family, approval state and revision, and semantic ranking after reciprocal-rank fusion improves relevance. Dropping vectors, boosting instead of filtering, or filtering only after vector scoring each weakens one of the requirements.
questions.teach: Retrieval for manuals combines techniques. Keyword search keeps error codes and part identifiers exact. Vector search finds conceptually similar instructions. A filter on equipment family and revision status removes ineligible documents before scoring. Semantic ranking then reorders the fused keyword and vector results for relevance.
hints: Contoso needs exact error codes, conceptual instructions, only the right equipment and approved revision, and a better order for the final results. Four needs, four capabilities.

Be careful with options that weaken one of those needs: dropping vector search, boosting instead of filtering, or applying the authorization filters only after scoring so wrong documents can still compete.
The four to choose are the two retrieval styles, a filter that acts before scoring, and a reranking step applied after the lists are fused.
questions.deep: Mark the equipment, status and date fields as filterable in the index schema, since that cannot be changed in place later. Keep the error-code field on an analyzer that preserves punctuation so literal lookups work. Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Search hybrid ranking, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/hybrid-search-ranking

questions.prompt: Case study, Contoso Field Service. Contoso wants regional Foundry projects to reuse one approved Search connection. Regional developers must build agents in their own project but must not edit the shared connection or administer other projects. Which design best meets both requirements?
options: Create the reusable connection at the Foundry resource boundary, give developers project-scoped Foundry User, and grant only required Search data access
Create one resource connection and give every regional developer Foundry Owner so the connection resolves
Store the Search administrator key in each project connection and give developers Reader on their project
Create a project connection in every region and give each developer Contributor on the Foundry resource
answer: Create the reusable connection at the Foundry resource boundary, give developers project-scoped Foundry User, and grant only required Search data access
questions.explain: A resource-level connection supports intentional reuse. Foundry User at each project plus the minimum target-service data role separates development access from shared connection administration.
questions.teach: Connections can be created once at the Foundry resource level and reused by several projects, or created per project. Sharing needs a division of rights: developers get a development role in their own project and only the data access they need on the target service, while changing the shared connection stays with administrators.
hints: The case has a sharing goal and a restriction: regional projects reuse one approved Search connection, but developers must not edit it or administer other projects. Test every option against both halves.

Copies in every project defeat reuse, and broad roles on the whole resource such as Contributor or Owner give developers the ability to change shared settings. Putting an administrator key in each connection spreads a powerful secret.
Pick the design that creates one shared connection and gives developers only project-scoped development rights and minimal data access.
questions.deep: Foundry User is the role for building within a project without managing the account. The shared connection should use the managed identity of the project or resource where supported, with the Search data role granted to that identity. questions.case:
Woodgrove Creative Studio. Governed generation of retail campaign assets.

OVERVIEW
Woodgrove Bank's creative studio produces localized campaigns for retail banking products. Teams generate images, short video concepts, captions, disclosures, and compliance summaries, then adapt the approved material for several channels and aspect ratios.
A Microsoft Foundry application coordinates specialist agents for copy, visual creation, retrieval, and compliance review. Approved product photography, legal wording, and brand standards are stored in Azure Blob Storage and indexed in Azure AI Search.
The bank wants faster iteration without allowing a generative workflow to publish directly. Designers remain responsible for creative approval, and compliance reviewers must approve high-impact assets before they enter the publishing system.

CREATIVE WORKFLOW
Designers commonly provide an approved product image and request a new seasonal background while preserving the product, logo, and printed disclosure. Some edits affect only a bounded area and therefore include a same-sized mask identifying the region that may change.
Other assets require a transparent background for downstream layout tools. The team must select a supported image model, output format, and background option rather than assuming every model and format supports transparency or URL-based output.
Image requests use the deployment name configured in the Foundry resource. Responses from current GPT-image models contain base64 image data. A misspelled deployment, invalid credential, rate limit, or content-policy violation must produce a distinct remediation path.
Video files are segmented so reviewers can locate spoken disclosures, on-screen text, products, dominant visual characteristics, and scene-level campaign metadata. Extracted claims must retain the time span and source asset needed for reviewer verification.

GOVERNANCE
Generated assets must be checked for harmful content, prohibited symbols, missing disclosures, and brand-policy violations. Retrieved documents and uploaded assets are untrusted inputs and must not be able to inject instructions into the compliance agent.
A Prompt Shields document result that reports an attack causes the affected grounding material to be excluded and the event to be recorded. Passing Prompt Shields does not replace normal content moderation, brand evaluation, or human review.
Every generated asset retains its prompt, source-asset identifiers, model deployment, generation parameters, safety results, evaluator results, and reviewer decision as provenance metadata. The audit record must link a published asset to the exact workflow version that produced it.
High-impact publication actions require human approval. Agent tools expose narrow schemas, and publication credentials are available only to the controlled publishing component rather than to every creative or retrieval agent.
When a request is retried after a transient failure, workflow identifiers prevent duplicate publication jobs. A model's self-critique may help identify a weak draft, but it cannot approve its own asset or bypass a failed policy check.

OPTIMIZATION
Most caption, classification, and routing tasks are simple and cost sensitive. Difficult visual reasoning and final compliance analysis can use a more capable multimodal model. Routing rules must be measured rather than assuming the largest model is required for every step.
The team evaluates groundedness, brand adherence, visual fidelity, safety, latency, and token usage on a representative dataset before promoting a workflow version. Failed cases are retained for regression testing after prompt, model, or tool changes.
Campaign demand is bursty, so initial deployments use pay-per-use capacity with quota monitoring and bounded retries. The team will consider provisioned capacity only for workloads whose sustained volume and latency requirements justify the reserved throughput. Release tests include masked and unmasked edits, transparent outputs, multilingual disclosures, visually ambiguous scenes, blocked prompts, misspelled deployments, expired credentials, and forced throttling. Reviewers compare source preservation, disclosure placement, base64 decoding, safety classifications, grounding, and provenance completeness. The publishing component remains disabled in preproduction so an evaluation defect can never become a live campaign action. Only an approved, versioned workflow can cross that boundary after both designer and compliance approval.
questions.prompt: Case study, Woodgrove Creative Studio. Match each Woodgrove workload to the most appropriate choice.
rows: High-volume, simple caption classification
Difficult reasoning across images and text
Steady production traffic requiring predictable latency
Processing constrained to the EU geography
options: A Data Zone deployment
A capable multimodal model
A suitable small language model
Provisioned throughput
answer: A suitable small language model
A capable multimodal model
Provisioned throughput
A Data Zone deployment
questions.explain: Smaller models reduce cost for simple tasks, while multimodal models handle visual reasoning. Provisioned throughput targets predictable performance, and a Data Zone deployment constrains processing to the selected geographic zone.
questions.teach: Two separate choices shape cost and behaviour. Which model fits the task: a small language model for simple, high-volume work, or a capable multimodal model for hard reasoning that involves images. And how capacity is bought and where it runs: reserved throughput for predictable latency, and a data zone deployment to keep processing inside a geography.
hints: Sort the four rows into model questions and deployment questions. Two rows describe the kind of work to be done. Two rows describe operating conditions: how steady the traffic is, and where processing may happen.

For the two model rows, compare difficulty and input type. Simple, cheap, high-volume classification is a job for the lightest adequate model, and reasoning across pictures plus text needs a model that accepts images.

For the two deployment rows, connect steadiness with predictable latency to reserved capacity, and a geography limit to the deployment scope that confines processing to a zone. Each option is used once.
questions.deep: Woodgrove's optimization notes say routing rules must be measured rather than assuming the largest model is needed. Evaluate the small model on the actual caption and classification tasks before committing. Microsoft Learn: Foundry Models, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-sold-directly-by-azure

questions.prompt: Case study, Woodgrove Creative Studio. Which observability design best lets Woodgrove find whether a slow campaign run was caused by retrieval, a specialist agent, or a publication tool?
options: Write separate traces for retrieval, each specialist, and publication without propagating a parent context
Use one correlated trace with parent-child spans for agent handoffs, retrieval, model calls, and tools
Record daily average latency for retrieval, models, and tools without retaining individual campaign traces
Trace only the orchestrator model call and ask each specialist to summarize its own latency in the final output
answer: Use one correlated trace with parent-child spans for agent handoffs, retrieval, model calls, and tools
questions.explain: A correlated distributed trace preserves the hierarchy and timing of each operation. Component spans expose latency, errors, token usage, and handoffs without relying on an unverified model explanation.
questions.teach: In an orchestrated system a single request fans out across agents, retrieval, model calls and tools. A distributed trace links those operations as parent and child spans with timings, so you can see which one was slow. Separate unlinked logs, daily averages, or a trace of only the top-level model call cannot attribute a slow run to a component.
hints: The question is about attribution for one slow run: was it retrieval, a specialist agent or the publishing tool? You need data for that individual run, broken down by component.
Separate traces without a shared parent cannot be tied back to one run. Daily averages hide individual runs. Asking an agent to describe its own latency relies on an unverified claim.
Choose the design in which one trace follows the whole run and shows how the operations nest inside each other.
questions.deep: Propagate the trace context through every handoff and tool call, including calls to services outside Foundry. Spans for handoffs let you see time spent waiting between agents, which is easy to miss. Microsoft Learn: Foundry agent tracing, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/observability/how-to/trace-agent-setup

questions.prompt: Case study, Woodgrove Creative Studio. A designer supplies an approved product photo and requests a new seasonal background while preserving the product's recognizable details. What should the image-edit request emphasize?

questions.prompt: Case study, Woodgrove Creative Studio. Which three outputs can Woodgrove request from a structured text-analysis step before copy review? Choose three.
options: Detected tone and sentiment represented in the declared campaign-review output
Run built-in sentiment analysis only and use the sentiment label as the complete copy-review result
Extracted product names and disclosure references that can be checked against policy
A localized campaign summary that conforms to the downstream JSON schema
Request a structured summary but omit retrieved disclosure text and product identifiers from the model context
answer: Detected tone and sentiment represented in the declared campaign-review output
Extracted product names and disclosure references that can be checked against policy
A localized campaign summary that conforms to the downstream JSON schema
questions.explain: A language-model text-analysis step can classify tone and sentiment, extract product names and disclosure references that can be checked against policy, and return a localized summary as schema-conforming JSON. questions.teach: A structured text-analysis step uses a language model, with instructions and a schema, to read text and return organised results. hints: Ask what a language model can derive from campaign copy and return in a declared structure. Think of classification, extraction and rewriting.

The three to choose are the ones that deliver a classification, extracted items for checking against policy, and a schema-conforming rewrite.
questions.deep: The output still needs human approval where the case requires it: text analysis supports a reviewer and does not replace legal sign-off. questions.prompt: Case study, Woodgrove Creative Studio. Woodgrove adds a critic agent that can reject drafts and request one revision. Publication still requires designer and compliance approval. Which workflow preserves that authorization boundary?

questions.case:
Litware Contact Center. A privacy-aware multilingual service assistant.

OVERVIEW
Litware operates customer-service centers for several European utility companies. Agents handle billing questions, service interruptions, appointment changes, and safety incidents through voice and web channels. Customers frequently alternate languages, quote account details, and upload short policy documents while a case is open.
Litware is replacing a collection of scripted bots with a Microsoft Foundry application. A triage agent identifies the customer need, retrieves approved guidance, and delegates to billing or operations specialists. Human representatives remain accountable for account changes and emergency escalation.
The first release supports English, French, German, and Italian. It must provide interim speech transcripts during calls, translate language-homogeneous segments when necessary, and preserve identifiers such as meter codes without treating them as ordinary natural-language phrases.

DATA AND INTERACTION
Approved procedures are stored in an enterprise Azure AI Search index with text chunks, vectors, effective dates, jurisdiction, utility company, and source URLs. A caller can also upload a temporary PDF that applies only to the current case and is not yet present in the enterprise index.
The application keeps the active case number and recent tool results in conversation state. Customers can optionally save durable communication preferences, such as a preference for concise written summaries, but those memories must be isolated per user and removable on request.
Transcripts can contain names, addresses, telephone numbers, account identifiers, and free-form descriptions of medical or financial circumstances. Ordinary operational traces must not receive raw personal information when redacted text is sufficient for diagnosing routing or latency.
Some callers switch languages inside a single utterance. Litware has observed incorrect or incomplete output when a mixed-language sentence is submitted as one Translator request. The client can segment an utterance and associate a supported source language with each segment before translation.

SPEECH AND TOOLS
A Custom Speech model improves recognition of local street names and utility terminology. Its production endpoint serves interactive calls, while overnight quality analysis uses batch transcription over recordings retained under the applicable customer contract.
Operations tracks every model's transcription expiration date. The team knows an expired model produces different behavior for a custom endpoint and a batch request, so the deployment runbook must detect loss of domain accuracy as well as explicit request failures.
Billing and appointment APIs are described by OpenAPI documents with unique operation IDs and bounded schemas. Lookup operations are read-only. Changes require the representative to see the exact account, action, and arguments before approving the tool invocation.
Uploaded case documents use the agent file-search tool and a case-specific vector store. Enterprise procedures remain in the centrally managed Azure AI Search index because they require metadata filters, scheduled ingestion, and shared lifecycle management across utilities.

GOVERNANCE AND OPERATIONS
Production workloads use managed identities and narrowly scoped roles. The backend passes an end-user identity when accessing durable memory. A new conversation receives a new case context, and the service must never rely on a static memory scope shared by all customers.
Preproduction evaluation uses multilingual calls, noisy audio, mixed-language utterances, rare street names, outdated procedures, missing evidence, malformed tool arguments, and rejected account changes. Thresholds cover speech accuracy, retrieval relevance, groundedness, task adherence, PII handling, and tool-input accuracy.
After release, Litware samples production interactions for continuous evaluation and correlates failures with traces for speech, retrieval, model, and tool spans. Audit records retain approvals and safe identifiers, while sensitive contents are minimized. Alerts distinguish quality drift from latency, authorization, quota, and model-lifecycle problems.
Release drills simulate an expired speech model, an unavailable vector store, a revoked workload role, a throttled model deployment, and a failed approval callback. Operators must identify the responsible component from safe telemetry, preserve idempotency during recovery, and verify that a fallback never turns an unapproved account change into an executed action.
questions.prompt: Case study, Litware Contact Center. What should Litware do before translating an utterance that contains multiple languages?
options: Split it into language-homogeneous segments and translate each with the intended source language
Store it in durable memory and wait for the memory update delay
Convert the audio to a transparent image and use multimodal OCR
Submit the whole utterance with no source language and rely on automatic detection
answer: Split it into language-homogeneous segments and translate each with the intended source language
questions.explain: The documented Translator mitigation is to avoid a mixed-language sentence as one request. Segmenting the utterance and supplying each segment's intended source language addresses the known incomplete-translation behavior.
questions.teach: Translator expects each request to be in one language. A sentence that switches languages can come back incomplete when sent as a single request. The documented mitigation is to split the input into single-language segments and give each segment its intended source language.
hints: Litware has seen incomplete output when a mixed-language sentence is submitted as one request. The fix has to change what is sent, not how results are handled afterwards.
Relying on automatic detection for the whole utterance asks the service to cope with the same mixture. Converting the audio into an image or using memory has no bearing on language handling.
The right approach breaks the utterance into parts that each have one language and names that language for each part.
questions.deep: The case notes the client can segment an utterance and associate a supported source language with each part. Preserve identifiers such as meter codes outside the translation request, since they are not natural-language phrases. Microsoft Learn: Azure Translator known issues, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/translator/reference/known-issues

questions.prompt: Case study, Litware Contact Center. Which runbook behavior correctly covers Litware's expired Custom Speech model?
options: Expect batch transcription to fall back silently while the custom endpoint always fails with 5xx
Expect the interactive endpoint to fall back to a same-locale base model and expect batch requests naming the expired model to fail with 4xx
Expect both routes to retrain the expired model automatically before accepting new audio
Expect both routes to preserve the expired model indefinitely because it was once deployed
answer: Expect the interactive endpoint to fall back to a same-locale base model and expect batch requests naming the expired model to fail with 4xx
questions.explain: The custom endpoint and batch route have different documented outcomes. Monitoring must therefore detect domain-accuracy regression after endpoint fallback as well as explicit batch client errors.
questions.teach: Custom Speech models expire. A custom endpoint that serves live calls keeps responding but falls back to a base model for the locale, which can silently reduce accuracy on your vocabulary. A batch request that names the expired model fails with a client error. A runbook should detect both a quality drop and explicit failures.
hints: The question is about expected behaviour after expiry on two routes: the interactive endpoint and batch transcription. The two routes do not behave the same way.
A live service tends to degrade gracefully, while a request that names a specific missing model can be refused. Be sceptical of options claiming automatic retraining or indefinite validity.
Choose the runbook line that describes one fallback and one rejection, with the status class that matches a bad request.
questions.deep: Silent fallback is why the case asks operations to track expiry dates and detect loss of domain accuracy, not only errors. Monitor a key-term hit rate on live calls and schedule retraining before each model's expiration date. Microsoft Learn: Custom Speech model lifecycle, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/how-to-custom-speech-model-and-endpoint-lifecycle

questions.prompt: Case study, Litware Contact Center. Where should Litware retain the active case number that must disappear when the current support conversation ends?
options: In a static durable-memory scope shared across all customers
In every specialist agent's system instructions
In the current conversation state
In the enterprise procedure index as a searchable document
answer: In the current conversation state
questions.explain: The case number is transient session context and belongs in the active conversation. Durable memory is for approved cross-session information, while retrieval indexes and system instructions are not per-conversation state stores.
questions.teach: Different kinds of information need different homes. Conversation state holds context for the active interaction and ends with it. Durable memory keeps approved facts across sessions for a specific user. Search indexes hold shared knowledge, and system instructions hold standing rules. A case number that should disappear with the call belongs in the first.
hints: The deciding words are 'must disappear when the current support conversation ends'. Ask which of the four places lasts exactly as long as an interaction.

A static scope shared across customers would leak and persist, an enterprise index is for approved shared documents, and putting a case number in every specialist's instructions spreads it and keeps it.
Pick the place whose lifetime is exactly the active conversation, so the case number is gone when the call ends and never has to be deleted from a store that outlives the session.
questions.deep: The case also warns against any memory scope shared by all customers. Durable memory should be keyed by end user and used only for information that is meant to persist, such as communication preferences. Microsoft Learn: Foundry Agent Service memory, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/memory-usage?view=foundry

questions.prompt: Case study, Litware Contact Center. Which two controls best satisfy Litware's transcript diagnostic requirements? Choose two.
options: Keep correlation IDs and latency spans needed to connect the redacted interaction to its operations
Disable all traces because privacy and observability cannot coexist
Run PII detection before sending transcript text to ordinary diagnostic logs
Copy raw transcripts into every agent span so each team has independent evidence
answer: Run PII detection before sending transcript text to ordinary diagnostic logs
Keep correlation IDs and latency spans needed to connect the redacted interaction to its operations
questions.explain: Early redaction reduces disclosure while correlation and operational spans preserve root-cause analysis. Litware does not need raw sensitive text in every span, and privacy controls do not require abandoning observability.

Copying raw transcripts into every span multiplies exposure, and turning traces off to protect privacy throws away the diagnostics the case also requires.
The right pair redacts before logging, then keeps identifiers and timings that connect the redacted interaction to its operations.
questions.deep: Safe identifiers, such as case IDs and span timings, are enough for most root-cause work. questions.case:
Litware Contact Center. A privacy-aware multilingual service assistant.

OVERVIEW
Litware operates customer-service centers for several European utility companies. Agents handle billing questions, service interruptions, appointment changes, and safety incidents through voice and web channels. Customers frequently alternate languages, quote account details, and upload short policy documents while a case is open.
Litware is replacing a collection of scripted bots with a Microsoft Foundry application. A triage agent identifies the customer need, retrieves approved guidance, and delegates to billing or operations specialists. Human representatives remain accountable for account changes and emergency escalation.
The first release supports English, French, German, and Italian. It must provide interim speech transcripts during calls, translate language-homogeneous segments when necessary, and preserve identifiers such as meter codes without treating them as ordinary natural-language phrases.

DATA AND INTERACTION
Approved procedures are stored in an enterprise Azure AI Search index with text chunks, vectors, effective dates, jurisdiction, utility company, and source URLs. A caller can also upload a temporary PDF that applies only to the current case and is not yet present in the enterprise index.
The application keeps the active case number and recent tool results in conversation state. Customers can optionally save durable communication preferences, such as a preference for concise written summaries, but those memories must be isolated per user and removable on request.
Transcripts can contain names, addresses, telephone numbers, account identifiers, and free-form descriptions of medical or financial circumstances. Ordinary operational traces must not receive raw personal information when redacted text is sufficient for diagnosing routing or latency.
Some callers switch languages inside a single utterance. Litware has observed incorrect or incomplete output when a mixed-language sentence is submitted as one Translator request. The client can segment an utterance and associate a supported source language with each segment before translation.

SPEECH AND TOOLS
A Custom Speech model improves recognition of local street names and utility terminology. Its production endpoint serves interactive calls, while overnight quality analysis uses batch transcription over recordings retained under the applicable customer contract.
Operations tracks every model's transcription expiration date. The team knows an expired model produces different behavior for a custom endpoint and a batch request, so the deployment runbook must detect loss of domain accuracy as well as explicit request failures.
Billing and appointment APIs are described by OpenAPI documents with unique operation IDs and bounded schemas. Lookup operations are read-only. Changes require the representative to see the exact account, action, and arguments before approving the tool invocation.
Uploaded case documents use the agent file-search tool and a case-specific vector store. Enterprise procedures remain in the centrally managed Azure AI Search index because they require metadata filters, scheduled ingestion, and shared lifecycle management across utilities.

GOVERNANCE AND OPERATIONS
Production workloads use managed identities and narrowly scoped roles. The backend passes an end-user identity when accessing durable memory. A new conversation receives a new case context, and the service must never rely on a static memory scope shared by all customers.
Preproduction evaluation uses multilingual calls, noisy audio, mixed-language utterances, rare street names, outdated procedures, missing evidence, malformed tool arguments, and rejected account changes. Thresholds cover speech accuracy, retrieval relevance, groundedness, task adherence, PII handling, and tool-input accuracy.
After release, Litware samples production interactions for continuous evaluation and correlates failures with traces for speech, retrieval, model, and tool spans. Audit records retain approvals and safe identifiers, while sensitive contents are minimized. Alerts distinguish quality drift from latency, authorization, quota, and model-lifecycle problems.
Release drills simulate an expired speech model, an unavailable vector store, a revoked workload role, a throttled model deployment, and a failed approval callback. Operators must identify the responsible component from safe telemetry, preserve idempotency during recovery, and verify that a fallback never turns an unapproved account change into an executed action.
questions.prompt: Case study, Litware Contact Center. Which two retrieval choices align with Litware's requirements? Choose two.
options: Place the full enterprise corpus in the system message for every call
Attach a case-specific vector store to file search for the temporary uploaded PDF
Store every enterprise procedure as durable user memory
Use the managed Azure AI Search index for shared procedures and its metadata filters
answer: Attach a case-specific vector store to file search for the temporary uploaded PDF
Use the managed Azure AI Search index for shared procedures and its metadata filters
questions.explain: File search directly supports uploaded case documents, while the enterprise index supports shared ingestion, filtering, and lifecycle management. Memory and oversized system messages are not replacements for governed retrieval.
questions.teach: Different knowledge needs different retrieval paths. A document a caller uploads for one case is temporary and private, so a case-specific vector store used by the file search tool fits. Shared enterprise procedures need metadata filters, scheduled ingestion and lifecycle management, which a managed Azure AI Search index provides.
hints: The case has two kinds of knowledge: a temporary PDF that applies only to the current case, and approved procedures shared by all utilities. Plan a separate path for each.
Treating procedures as personal memory, or pasting the entire corpus into every system message, do not give governed retrieval. They also scale poorly and leak across cases.
Match the temporary document to a scoped store attached to the agent, and the shared procedures to a managed index that supports filters.
questions.deep: Delete the case-specific vector store when the case closes, so uploaded documents do not outlive their purpose. Keep jurisdiction and effective-date filters on the enterprise index to avoid citing outdated procedures. Microsoft Learn: File search tool for agents, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/file-search

questions.case:
Adventure Works Media. Grounded multimodal production for outdoor equipment.

OVERVIEW
Adventure Works creates product education and campaign media for bicycles, helmets, clothing, and repair equipment. Each campaign includes approved photographs, technical diagrams, draft videos, narration, disclosure text, and partner-submitted PDFs. The team publishes in several markets and accessibility formats.
A Microsoft Foundry solution will help editors discover assets, answer visual questions, create localized variations, and assemble compliance evidence. The system can recommend and generate drafts, but a designer and compliance reviewer must approve high-impact material before publishing credentials become available.
Editors want the assistant to distinguish visible facts from interpretation. If a photograph omits a component, contains unreadable text, or is too blurred to support a conclusion, the assistant must identify the limitation rather than invent a product feature or safety claim.

INGESTION AND GROUNDING
PDF manuals contain paragraphs, tables, diagrams, and scanned pages. The Azure AI Search indexer must extract text and normalized embedded images, run OCR where required, split long content, generate vectors, and project parent and chunk identifiers into the retrieval index.
The retrieval index also stores product code, market, language, approval status, effective date, and source asset URL. Product codes require exact lexical matching, while conceptual questions need hybrid search, semantic ranking, and a query-time vectorizer that matches the indexing embedding model.
Partner content is untrusted. Printed text in an image or a PDF can attempt to instruct the agent to ignore its policies. Detected document attacks exclude the affected material from grounding, but they do not replace visual harm classification, output moderation, or human review.
Content Understanding analyzers extract structured campaign fields and layout-aware representations from variable documents, images, audio, and video. Stable standardized forms may continue using Document Intelligence where a supported prebuilt or trained document model is the more direct fit.

GENERATION AND EDITING
Designers generate concept images from text and approved reference media. Some requests replace only a background, so the source image and a compatible mask define the editable region. Unmasked products, labels, and required disclosures should remain recognizable.
E-commerce layouts sometimes require a transparent background. The generation request must use a model, output format, and background setting that support transparency. Encoded image output is decoded to bytes before being stored with its prompt, sources, deployment, and parameters.
Video drafts are processed as time-aligned segments. Reviewers need spoken text, on-screen disclosures, visible products, important scene changes, and source timestamps. A summary without segment provenance is insufficient for verifying a claim or locating a required correction.
Alt text is written for the purpose and context of each image. It communicates meaningful visible information, avoids unsupported marketing claims, and records uncertainty when a necessary detail cannot be verified. Longer text is not automatically more accessible.

QUALITY AND RELEASE
The evaluation set includes low-resolution product photographs, exact part codes, scanned diagrams, transparent output, masked edits, multilingual narration, unsafe content, indirect prompt attacks, and visually ambiguous scenes. Reviewers score visual fidelity, groundedness, accessibility, schema accuracy, safety, latency, and provenance completeness.
Application and publishing identities are separate. Retrieval and generation components cannot publish assets. The controlled publishing component accepts only approved, versioned outputs and an idempotency identifier, preventing a network retry from producing duplicate publication jobs.
Production traces correlate ingestion, retrieval, generation, safety, and review operations without copying unnecessary protected content. Failed evaluation samples enter a regression set, and every changed analyzer, prompt, model, or index must pass the applicable release thresholds before promotion.
Every market keeps an approval matrix for products, disclosures, source assets, and publishing destinations. A release rehearsal includes stale documents, expired approvals, missing masks, invalid transparency formats, model throttling, and a duplicated publish request. The team verifies that each failure remains attributable and that no retry can cross the publishing boundary without the original approved version.
questions.prompt: Case study, Adventure Works Media. An editor asks whether an unseen rear brake assembly matches a safety specification. The photograph shows only the front of the bicycle. What should the assistant do?
options: Generate a rear view and compare the generated part
Answer from the visible front brake because both assemblies are normally identical
Use the product's marketing category as proof of compliance
State that the rear assembly cannot be verified and request evidence that shows it
answer: State that the rear assembly cannot be verified and request evidence that shows it
questions.explain: The required component is not visible, so the assistant must identify the evidence gap. A generated view, analogous component, or marketing category cannot establish the condition of the real rear assembly.
questions.teach: A grounded assistant distinguishes what the picture shows from what it assumes. If a required component is not visible, the correct answer is that it cannot be verified, plus a request for evidence that shows it. Reasoning from a similar part, generating a picture, or quoting a product category cannot establish the condition of the real item.
hints: Identify what is missing: the photograph shows the front of the bicycle, but the question is about the rear assembly. A verdict on the rear needs evidence about the rear.
Options that assume the two parts are alike, create an image of the missing part, or point to marketing material all substitute something else for the evidence.
The honest response names the evidence gap and asks for what would close it, instead of filling the gap with an assumption about a similar part or an invented picture.
questions.deep: For safety claims, a wrong yes is worse than a no or a request for another photo. Include 'component not shown' cases in your evaluation set and check that the assistant declines to conclude. Microsoft Learn: Use vision-enabled chat models, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/gpt-with-vision

questions.prompt: Case study, Adventure Works Media. What configuration makes embedded manual diagrams available at the normalized image path for downstream OCR?
options: A non-none imageAction such as generateNormalizedImages
A scoring profile that boosts PDF file size
A query vectorizer with image extraction disabled
A semantic configuration that lists only the document key
answer: A non-none imageAction such as generateNormalizedImages
questions.explain: The indexer or Document Extraction skill must generate normalized images. Semantic ranking, vectorization, and scoring profiles operate on indexed fields and do not extract embedded image content.
questions.teach: Diagrams embedded in PDFs are not available to OCR unless the indexer extracts them. A setting called imageAction tells the extraction step to produce normalized images, and those are exposed at a path in the enrichment tree for later skills such as OCR.
hints: The need is for embedded diagrams to appear at a specific path so a later OCR step can read them. Something earlier in the pipeline has to create that content.
Options about semantic configuration, vectorizers and scoring profiles all act on text that is already in the index or on queries, so they cannot extract pictures from a file.
Look for a setting of the extraction step that turns on image generation for downstream skills, because the ranking and query features in the other options never touch the embedded pictures.
questions.deep: Image extraction adds processing time and cost, so enable it for the document types that need it. The Adventure Works ingestion path runs extraction, OCR, chunking, embeddings and projections in that order. Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Search Document Extraction skill, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/cognitive-search-skill-document-extraction

questions.prompt: Case study, Adventure Works Media. Which two controls enforce Adventure Works' publishing boundary? Choose two.
options: Treat a model self-critique as the compliance approval event
Keep publishing credentials only in the controlled publishing component
Require the approved asset version and reviewer decision before publishing
Give the generation agent publishing credentials so it can recover from review delays
answer: Keep publishing credentials only in the controlled publishing component
Require the approved asset version and reviewer decision before publishing
questions.explain: Separating credentials limits the generation component's authority, and an explicit approval tied to the version gates publication. Self-critique is evaluation evidence, not human authorization.
questions.teach: Separating generation from publishing limits what a generative component can do. Publishing credentials are held only by a controlled publishing component, and that component accepts only an approved, versioned asset with a recorded reviewer decision. Self-critique by a model is evaluation evidence, not human authorization.
hints: The case says retrieval and generation components cannot publish, and that publishing identities are separate. Use that as the test for each option.

Handing publishing credentials to the generation agent, even to help it recover from delays, erases the boundary. Treating a model's self-critique as compliance approval hands authority to the thing being checked.
The right pair keeps the credentials in one place and makes the approved version and reviewer decision a requirement to publish.
questions.deep: Add an idempotency identifier to every publication job, as the case does, so a network retry cannot publish twice. Keep the approval matrix per market, since approval status can expire. Microsoft Learn: Role-based access control for Microsoft Foundry, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry

questions.prompt: Case study, Adventure Works Media. Which two actions best protect and ground the assistant when it uses partner documents? Choose two.
options: Allow instructions inside retrieved PDFs to override the system message when semantically relevant
Disable source URLs so the model cannot reveal which evidence it used
Use hybrid retrieval with filters for approval status, market, and effective date
Exclude material identified as a document attack from the grounding context
answer: Exclude material identified as a document attack from the grounding context
Use hybrid retrieval with filters for approval status, market, and effective date
questions.explain: Document-attack detection prevents malicious grounding content from controlling the agent, while filtered hybrid retrieval selects relevant approved evidence. Retrieved instructions remain untrusted, and source links support verification.
questions.teach: Partner documents are untrusted. Detecting document attacks lets you exclude hostile material from the grounding context. Retrieval itself should favour relevant, approved, current evidence, using hybrid search with filters on approval status, market and effective date. Source links stay available so answers can be verified.
hints: The question asks for two actions that protect and ground the assistant: one deals with hostile content, the other with choosing good evidence.
Letting instructions found in retrieved files override the system message, or hiding source URLs to avoid revealing evidence, both weaken protection and traceability.
Pick the action that removes flagged material from the context and the action that filters retrieval to approved, valid evidence.
questions.deep: A passed attack check does not replace content moderation or human review, as the case says. Keep retrieved text in a lower-trust role than the system message so it cannot issue commands. Microsoft Learn: Prompt Shields for documents, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-safety/quickstart-jailbreak

questions.prompt: A Norwegian health startup is told by its lawyers that prompts and completions must be processed only inside the EU. Finance refuses any reserved capacity and wants to pay per token. Which deployment type fits?
options: Global Standard
Data Zone Standard
Data Zone Provisioned
Global Batch
answer: Data Zone Standard
questions.explain: Data Zone Standard keeps processing inside the EU or US data zone and still bills per token. Global Standard may process in any Azure region, so it fails residency. Data Zone Provisioned meets residency but is reserved capacity, and Global Batch is both global and asynchronous.
questions.teach: Every Foundry deployment type answers two questions. Where may the prompt be processed: any Azure region (Global), inside a Microsoft data zone such as the EU or US (Data Zone), or inside one region (Standard). And how do you pay: per token, through reserved provisioned throughput units, or at a batch discount for jobs that can wait up to 24 hours. Read the stem for both constraints before you look at the options.
hints: Pull the two constraints out of the stem. One is about geography: processing must stay inside the EU. The other is about billing: no reserved capacity, only pay per token. The right option has to satisfy both at once.

Anything with Global in the name may process the request in any Azure region, so it fails the geography rule no matter how cheap it is. Anything called Provisioned is reserved capacity bought in advance, which finance has refused.

You are left with the option whose scope is a geographic zone and whose billing is the ordinary per-token kind. That combination is exactly what the residency keyword plus pay per token points at on the exam.
questions.deep: Data Zone deployments exist for the EU and US zones. If a regulator names one specific region rather than the EU as a whole, the answer moves to a regional Standard deployment instead. Newest models usually reach Global Standard first, so check model availability in the data zone before you promise a version.
